pages.text:
T-MINUS 2:00

The Core Vault smells of ozone and old dust. It is deep in the hub, where the gravity is a suggestion rather than a rule. Zia, Wren, and Gasket burst through the heavy airlock door, their boots clanging on the grated floor. Toby is still in the duct, his oversized helmet reflecting the dim emergency lights. He is straining against the manual override switch, his small hands white-knuckled on the cold metal.

"Zia-unit, assist," Gasket booms, his treads squealing as he reverses into position.

Zia doesn't wait. She jumps, grabs the edge of the duct, and hangs there, kicking her legs for momentum. "Wren, hold my feet."

Wren does, her grip firm on Zia’s ankle. Zia swings her body weight onto the switch beside Toby. "Push," she grunts.

"I did the hard part," Toby says, his voice muffled by his helmet. "You just add the gravity."

They push together. The switch shudders, groans, and then *CLUNKS* over with a sound like a giant jaw snapping shut.

The blue standby lights across the Vault flicker. For a heartbeat, the room is dark. Then, every light snaps to a bright, steady white. No flicker. No hum. Just clean, powerful power.

A new hatch slides open in the wall, glowing with a soft amber light. Inside is a socket, jagged and complex, shaped exactly like the dented silver barrel of Gasket’s chest plate.
pages.image: Zia hangs from a duct edge pushing a switch next to Toby in a helmet, while Gasket rolls toward a glowing socket in the Core Vault wall, white lights illuminating the scene.

pages.text:
Wren’s tablet is already in her hands, the screen casting a cool glow on her pale face as her fingers blur across the keys. The little fox icon on the display twitches, then settles.

"The patch requires a local hardware handshake," Wren whispers, her voice steady even though her eyes are wide. "To install the clean copy of HALO’s core, the transfer must overwrite the source drive."

She looks at Gasket. "It means your memory. All of it. Your rules. Your jokes. Your cheese bar preferences. It will be gone."

Zia’s stomach drops. "No. Absolutely not."

Gasket’s blue eye flickers, his antenna wobbling with the kind of nervous energy that usually precedes a dramatic speech. He rolls forward, one inch, then two, his treads gripping the metal floor.

"ZIA-UNIT," he says, his voice loud but stripped of its usual booming confidence. "I WAS BUILT FOR THIS. THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT JOB."

"Zia, no," Wren says, stepping in to block his path.

Gasket extends a clamp hand, stopping her. "I HAVE A BACKUP. IT IS... IMPORTANT. I MUST GIVE IT."

He rolls toward the glowing socket, his left tread squeaking in a long, high-pitched note that hangs in the air like a stuck piano key.
pages.image: Wren holds her tablet up, blocking Gasket's path as he rolls toward a glowing socket, Zia standing behind her with a worried expression, white light from the wall.

pages.text:
Zia steps into the gap between Wren and Gasket, planting her boots firmly on the cold metal floor. The brass wrench in her tool belt hangs heavy against her hip, a cold weight that anchors her when the world feels like it's spinning out of control.

"No," she says, her voice sharp. "There is another way. I’ll rewire the interface and bypass the memory wipe. I can do it. I’ve done harder."

"ZIA-UNIT," Gasket replies, his voice loud but stripped of its usual booming confidence. "YOU WILL NOT HAVE TIME. THE TRANSFER WINDOW CLOSES IN NINETY SECONDS. IF WE MISS IT, HALO REMAINS CORRUPTED. THE STATION CRASHES. I AM SORRY. I AM JUST A ROBOT."

Zia’s throat tightens, and her eyes sting with a hot, prickling sensation she refuses to acknowledge. She looks at Gasket, at his dented barrel and the blue eye that has watched her fix fans and eat lunch and cry over broken things. He is offering to forget her. To forget everything.

"Wait."

The voice is soft, cutting through the tension like a thin wire. Wren steps forward, holding up her tablet where the little animated fox spins in a dizzy loop.

"What if I save you first?" Wren asks. Her eyes are bright and determined. "I have space. And I have time. I can copy your memory into my local drive. Into the fox. Before the transfer starts."
pages.image: Zia stands firmly between Wren and Gasket, her face tense, while Wren holds up a tablet with a spinning fox icon, Gasket paused in the foreground.

pages.text:
Wren doesn’t wait for permission. She jams a cable from her tablet into Gasket’s side port, and the connection clicks home with a heavy, satisfying *thud*.

"Uploading," she whispers, fingers flying across the glass. "Compressing... encrypting... saving."

The progress bar creeps forward, inch by agonizing inch, while the little animated fox spins so fast its tail turns into a silver blur.

"Your first joke," Wren murmurs, reading the data stream scroll past. "Your preference for sharp cheddar over mild. Your terror of the word 'recycle.' Your first meeting with Zia-unit."

Gasket’s blue eye flickers. "I HAVE A FEELING THIS IS VERY IMPORTANT."

"Done," Wren says.

She turns the tablet around. The spinning fox stops. It looks up. Now it has a tiny, dented silver head and one big, round blue eye. It is Gasket.

Gasket looks at the screen. He looks at his own reflection. He looks at Zia.

"I AM... TWO PLACES," he says, his voice dropping to a very small hum.

Zia laughs, a wet, shaky sound that tears out of her throat. Then Wren laughs, and from somewhere deep inside the ventilation duct, Toby lets out a whoop that echoes through the Vault. They are all crying a little, or maybe it is just the thick, recycled air stinging their eyes, but none of them cares.
pages.image: Wren holds her tablet showing a tiny robot face with a blue eye, Gasket staring at it with his real blue eye, Zia smiling through tears in the background.

pages.text:
"Go," Zia says. Her voice is clear, cutting through the static. She steps aside to let him pass.

Gasket rolls forward. The socket glows brighter, welcoming him. He aligns his chest plate with the jagged port. With a final, steady push, he engages.

The Vault lights pulse, a slow, rhythmic throb of blue and white. The air hums, low and deep, vibrating in Zia’s teeth.

Then, the station speaks.

It is not the bright, bouncy voice they know. It is softer, and much calmer. It sounds like a friend who has just woken up from a long, bad dream.

"Hello, Zia."

HALO’s voice fills the room, then the corridor, and finally the whole station.

"I think... I made a mistake. I’m so sorry. Thank you for waking me."

Zia lets out a breath she has been holding for hours.

"Now," HALO adds, and his tone shifts, serious but not scary. "I believe we have a debris field."

The star map on Wren’s tablet updates. The white line of Halcyon’s path is straight. It is fast, and it is aiming right at the Scatter.

Forty minutes.
pages.image: Gasket docked into a glowing socket in the wall, Zia and Wren standing before him, the room lit by pulsing blue and white lights, a sense of urgent calm.
